subject: Security intake: SOC2 Type II, bridge letter & Trust Portal access
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@paymentsync.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: security discovery & SOC 2 artifacts (next steps)

Alex — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock the trial/POC: 

Summary of call:
- PaymentSync is evaluating Redwood for real-time payment description generation (low latency, sensitive PII fields)
- Key controls discussed: encryption at rest, tokenization, audit logs, and data retention

Requested artifacts / actions from Redwood:
1) SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) + bridge letter that explicitly calls out encryption and key management language
2) Trust Portal access so your security team can download artifacts and start the vendor questionnaire (we host VSQ/DPQ there)
3) Answers to high-level GDPR/HIPAA posture questions (data residency & processing, subprocessors)

What we will provide: 
- I can upload a redacted SOC 2 Type II and a short bridge letter.
- I will provision Trust Portal access for PaymentSync security and attach the DPQ/VSQ in the portal. Invite will be live for 30 days.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Fri): I send bridge letter + redacted report and invite to Trust Portal
- Early next week: your team starts VSQ; we triage any follow-ups in GitHub-style threads in the portal

Attachments: redwood_soc2_factsheet.pdf (quick summary)

If you prefer, I can also route the artifacts through DocuSign for an access agreement; otherwise portal access requires a short acceptance form. Let me know which security contacts should receive the invite (I included "security-ops@paymentsync.com" as discussed).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0123
From: Alex Li <alex.li@paymentsync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@paymentsync.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: security discovery & SOC 2 artifacts (next steps)

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before you send: 

- SOC 2: we need the Type II report covering the last 12 months; redacted is fine but please include the report date range and auditor name
- Bridge letter: please include a short statement on encryption at rest, KMS/HSM usage, and whether customer-managed keys are supported
- GDPR/HIPAA: can you confirm if Redwood is comfortable signing a DPA that includes standard SCCs and the HIPAA BA terms?

We'd like Trust Portal access for these individuals:
- Alex Li <alex.li@paymentsync.com>
- security-ops@paymentsync.com

I've attached our initial DPQ file (paymentsync_dpq_v1.xlsx) with a handful of high-priority questions. If you prefer to import it into your portal rather than edit the Excel, happy either way.

Also please include any common AWS region residency commitments (we need to know if data can be kept in us-west-2).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Li
Senior Security Engineer
PaymentSync Inc.
alex.li@paymentsync.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@paymentsync.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: security discovery & SOC 2 artifacts (next steps)

Alex — thanks, and great questions. Short answers below and I've attached the artifacts to this email and uploaded them to the Trust Portal link.

Answers (brief):
- SOC 2 Type II: latest report covers 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31, auditor: Harland & Lee LLP. Redacted copy attached (redwood_soc2_2026_typeii_redacted.pdf).
- Bridge letter: attached (redwood_bridge_letter_2027.pdf). It calls out AES-256 at rest, KMS with HSM-backed keys, and the option for customer-managed keys via our dedicated/private deployment.
- GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood provides a standard DPA (SCCs included) and supports HIPAA BA terms for private deployments; we can route the DPA through DocuSign if that's easiest.
- Region / residency: we can commit to keeping Production data in us-west-2 for the POC and provide region-specific routing for Dedicated/Private customers.

Trust Portal invite: sent to alex.li@paymentsync.com and security-ops@paymentsync.com — access link: https://trust.redwood.com/invite/PSYNC-7f3a (expires in 30 days). Once you accept, you can download artifacts and start the VSQ; I imported the paymentsync_dpq_v1.xlsx into the portal for you.

Attachments included in portal and email: redwood_bridge_letter_2027.pdf, redwood_soc2_2026_typeii_redacted.pdf.

If you want a short 15-min sync next week to walk through any VSQ answers, Monica (cc'd) can take the lead.

Thanks,
Marcus
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Alex Li <alex.li@paymentsync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@paymentsync.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: security discovery & SOC 2 artifacts (next steps)

Marcus — confirmed access and downloaded the materials. Quick follow-ups for the VSQ team: 

1) Data residency: confirmed we'll keep POC data in us-west-2; can you confirm retention defaults and whether retention policy can be shortened to 30 days for the trial?
2) Audit logs: do you provide per-tenant audit logs with token-level tracing, and are they accessible via the Console/API?

We should be set to start the DPQ this afternoon. Monica — Lauren, can we schedule a 15-min call tomorrow to go over any sticky answers?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Security Engineer
PaymentSync Inc.
